extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature: scientists, students, and professional practitioners (early-20th-century) interested in scientific books, instruments, and reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and evaluative points for reviewing scientific books and instruments (book reviews and instrument notices) as presented in a Nature journal issue. Focuses on technical accuracy, experimental verification, scope, illustrations, authors' qualifications, and pedagogical usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental testing of results
rubrics_metrics.description: "the care with which the author has experimentally tested the results obtained"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive reviews note when theoretical work is accompanied by experimental verification (example cited p. 309). Experimental testing that leads to extension or revision of theory is valued; absence of experimental checks weakens a theoretical presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of theory and practice
rubrics_metrics.description: "Throughout the book, theory and practice go hand in hand"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works that integrate theoretical treatment with practical application are praised; reviewers expect tangible, useful outcomes rather than purely abstract exercises. Books should show how theory informs real-world operations (recommended also for examinational emphasis).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and quantitative comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: "the argument is never pushed far enough to enable a quantitative comparison to be made"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims and explanations should be pushed to quantitative form where possible; vague or purely qualitative argumentation is criticized. Reviewers look for numerical/quantitative checks that allow comparison with established data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusive and well-supported reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: "the reasoning here appears to be scarcely conclusive"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments that rest on unexpressed assumptions or lack demonstration are viewed negatively. A reviewer expects clear chains of inference and evidence supporting asserted mechanisms or phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of the word 'law' / restraint in generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: "The term law appears to be used here in a somewhat unusual sense, as these statements do not constitute laws"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should avoid overstating generalizations; statements called 'laws' should be supported by clear functional relations or demonstrated dependence. Reviewers penalize inflated terminology unsupported by rigorous derivation or data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope, completeness and topical coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: e.g., "the work is almost entirely devoted to iron and steel founding" and remarks that "a few lines... might have been devoted to the moulds used for metals with low melting points..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A book titled 'General' is expected to cover its declared breadth; missing modern or relevant topics (e.g., modern bronze casting methods, plaster moulds, moulds for low-melting-point metals) is a point of criticism. Reviewers list chapter headings to assess completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Up-to-dateness / inclusion of modern practices
rubrics_metrics.description: "signs of progress... the field for machine moulding is extending. Permanent moulds made of carbon or similar material are being tried" contrasted with omissions (e.g., cire perdue process not mentioned)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers value inclusion and discussion of recent industry advances and modern techniques; omission of well-established contemporary methods is a negative, especially for practical handbooks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and selection of illustrations and printing
rubrics_metrics.description: "The illustrations, of which there are 246, have been carefully chosen, and, like the letterpress, are exceptionally well printed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality, well-chosen illustrations and clear printing are important for technical books; reviewers note number, selection, and print quality of figures as a positive feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors' qualifications and practical experience
rubrics_metrics.description: "The authors possess special qualifications for the work they have undertaken... Mr. Longmuir has held the position of foundry foreman... Mr. McWilliam... at the University of Sheffield had ample opportunity of ascertaining the needs of students."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers emphasize authors' professional background and direct practical experience as credentials that increase a work's authority and usefulness, especially for applied subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical accuracy and treatment of specialised detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: discussion of impurities in cast iron — "Phosphorus... increases the fluidity... Sulphur tends to make castings harder and brittle. Silicon... has a beneficent influence. Manganese... tends to keep carbon in the combined form."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate, specific treatment of technical details (metallurgical effects, impurities, mixing by analysis) is essential in practical reference works; reviewers look for correct facts and their practical implications for industry practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Level and intended readership / pedagogical suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Remarks such as "the special treatises on the subject are mostly of an elementary character" and recommendations that students should procure instruments or texts (e.g., Anglemeter) and that examiners should place more importance on practical geometrical optics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether a work's level (elementary, exhaustive, intermediate) matches its aims and audience. Pedagogical usefulness, suitability for examinations, and accessibility to students are important evaluative dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speculativeness vs. established explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticisms like "the reasoning is in general vague" and that many explanations "would follow from any theory... that assigns to it the fundamental properties of a moving system" indicate concern about speculative models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers distinguish between speculative, broad-reaching explanatory models and narrowly tested theories; speculative accounts need clearer demonstration and quantitative support before being accepted as satisfactory explanations of phenomena.
